A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SyncDiff and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original motion-synthesis evaluations on five datasets, component ablations, and a 150-participant user study.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds comparative inference timings and a qualitative finding about classifier-based evaluation.

M1.justification: The motion representation, frequency decomposition, diffusion architecture, losses, synchronization procedure, and mesh reconstruction remain unchanged. Introductory wording changes do not establish a procedural change given the retained equations and algorithms.

E1.justification: Both evaluate TACO, CORE4D, GRAB, OAKINK2, and BEHAVE with the same interaction configurations and generalization scenarios. The added timing and classifier analyses reuse existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Tables 8–9 add OMOMO, CG-HOI, MACS, and DiffH2O to runtime comparisons, whereas v3's timing comparisons concern SyncDiff and its synchronization variants. These methods already participate in synthesis-quality comparisons, whose comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 adds comparative timing of 200-frame sequences on a single NVIDIA A40 and reports a diagnostic using a classifier trained only on the training split. The main evaluation splits, training budgets, and RA classifier trained on combined train/validation/test data remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new timing tables extend the synchronization-cost comparison beyond the existing TACO interval sweep. Appendix E.2, question 6 adds a qualitative diagnostic of RA bias under training-only classifier fitting. Existing component, cutoff, and frequency-filtering ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The user-study sample size and voting procedure are unchanged, and the added results introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v5 adds baseline and unsynchronized inference times; for example, Table 8 reports CORE4D times of 7.1 seconds for OMOMO, 10.7 for CG-HOI, and 5.4 without synchronization. Full SyncDiff timings already appeared in v3 Table 18. Main benchmark scores and user-study votes are unchanged. Appendix E.2 newly reports that a training-only RA classifier scores some ground-truth test motions below baselines, without numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, alignment-score derivation, synchronization proof and assumptions in Appendix A are retained. Several displayed formulas become inline expressions or receive new numbers, without changing their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about generic multi-body synthesis, alignment-based synchronization, frequency decomposition, and superior contact and semantic quality. The introduction's average recognition-accuracy advantage of over 15% is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 adds substantive discussion of RA's preference for in-domain motions, the rationale for classifier training across splits, and possible mitigations. Appendix B.2 newly attributes runtime competitiveness to avoiding baseline-specific guidance or multiple synthesis stages. The cutoff rationale is also qualified relative to original motion amplitude.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly documents the comparative timing workload as 200-frame synthesis on one A40 and supplies baseline computational costs. A40 usage, SyncDiff resource costs, architecture and training hyperparameters, mesh-reconstruction details, and the project access link were already documented and remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 127 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Changed citation-page links reflect layout changes; the added runtime and evaluator discussions introduce no new cited work or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized prose and cross-reference edits, expands Appendix B.2, and adds a sixth discussion question in E.2. The section sequence and most prose remain intact. It fixes the unresolved metric-pseudocode reference but incorrectly changes the mesh-details reference from C.2 to B.2.

P2.justification: v5 adds two runtime tables and restyles existing tables with fewer gridlines, revised headers, and spacing changes. Table 5 and several figures move, and Figures 9–10 exchange numbering. All ten figure images, including the user-study chart, remain unchanged; the overall two-column layout is retained.

improvement.justification: The added baseline timings make computational competitiveness easier to assess, while the RA discussion makes evaluator bias more explicit. These provide limited benefits beyond v3's existing evidence. Qualifications remain: the classifier diagnostic lacks numerical support, and the new 'less than 25%' synchronization-cost statement is ambiguous—Table 9's 7.7 versus 5.9 seconds represents about a 31% increase over unsynchronized inference. Some cross-references also worsen.
